decisions.reason: Having survived its first full market test as a close-to-core design variant, it likely meets at least minimum aspirations and is inexpensive enough to retain within the firm's broad design-led range.

This shower channel remains tightly aligned with the firm's core drainage business and barrier-free bathroom trend, so absent clear performance failure management would keep it while refining sales and installation learning.

The pump-assisted line still carries the highest withdrawal risk because it is more complex and niche, but the firm's innovation capabilities and available slack make continued experimentation more likely than exit.
As a very natural extension of the established floor-drain portfolio, this product would usually stay unless results were clearly below aspiration, which there is no strong sign of here.
This design grate is a low-risk complementary offering that supports the firm's aesthetics-and-service positioning, so boundedly rational management is likely to leave it in the portfolio.

Because it is the newest and technically more specialized pump-based launch, uncertainty is still material, but in a growing market the firm is likely to give it more time before reallocating resources.
